[{"node":"loopar_website_menu_content","element":"menu_content","data":{"key":"loopar_website_menu_content","id":"loopar_website_menu_content","name":"loopar_website_menu_content"},"elements":[{"node":"website-overview","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Overview","key":"website-overview","id":"website-overview","name":"website-overview","value":"# Website

An app **has a website** when its **Has Website** switch is on. The App form's **Website** tab then holds everything public: menu, header (logo, position, solid/transparent, fixed), footer, copyright and theme. Pages are built with the **Page Builder** and reached through the menu.

| Menu row | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| **Page** | The page it opens — from **any** app installed in the tenant |
| **Link** | Its URL segment (`/about`) |
| **Parent menu** | Nest it under another row (sub-menus, docs sidebars) |
| **Router only** | Routable but not shown in the navigation (detail pages, signing page) |

Links resolve case- and separator-insensitively: `/getting-started`, `/Getting Started` and `/getting_started` reach the same row.

![One tenant serving several websites](/assets/public/multisite.svg)
"}},{"node":"website-multisite","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Several Websites","key":"website-multisite","id":"website-multisite","name":"website-multisite","value":"## Several Websites per Tenant

Informational sites rarely need a backend of their own. One tenant can serve **several websites**, each on its own domain and rendered by its own app, all managed from one Desk.

In **Tenant Manager**, list them in **Websites**, one per line, `domain = app`:

```
acme.com      = acme-site
shop.acme.com = acme-shop
blog.dev      = personal-blog
```

| Behavior | Detail |
|----------|--------|
| Routing | Each domain renders the web workspace of its app (menu, header, theme) |
| Pages | A site's menu can use pages from any app of the tenant — no isolation between apps, so several apps can contribute to one site |
| Local testing | Every website also answers on `<domain>.localhost` (`blog.dev.localhost`) — no DNS needed |
| Desk | **Not served** on website domains: `/desk` answers 404 (no redirect revealing where the administration lives). Administer everything from the tenant's main domain |
| Visitors | Web users can still sign in on website domains — comments, reviews and messages keep working |
| Caddy | Website domains are registered and get SSL like the main domain |
| Data | Contact messages record the site they came from; analytics record each page |
"}},{"node":"website-content","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Content","key":"website-content","id":"website-content","name":"website-content","value":"## Content Entities

The core app ships content types every site needs. Each belongs to an **app** (the website it appears on) and has a **Published** switch.

| Entity | For | Notable fields |
|--------|-----|----------------|
| **Post** | Blog / news | slug, author, published on, featured, reading time, summary, Markdown content, cover image, tags, canonical URL |
| **Project** · **Project Category** | Portfolio | client, dates, gallery, external URL, custom URL |
| **Service** · **Service Category** | Service catalog | tagline, deliverables / not included, pricing model (hidden, fixed, from, hourly, custom), price and unit, duration estimate, primary and secondary call to action |
| **Legal Notice** | Terms, privacy, cookies | slug, effective date, last updated, summary, Markdown content |
| **Announcement** | A bar at the top of the site | headline, message, link, starts/ends on, color (primary, accent, neutral), priority, *visitors can close it* |

Slugs are generated from the title and kept unique.

Show Posts, Projects, Services and Legal Notices with the **collection** (listing) and **collection_view** (detail page) elements — see [Components → Collections](/components). Their public data comes from public actions that only return published records of the current website.

### Announcements

The website shows the published announcement of its app whose dates include today — the highest priority first. When a visitor closes a dismissible announcement, it stays closed for them until you publish another.

### Comments and reviews

Entities with **Enable comments** get a thread on their public detail page (guest comments are held for approval; moderate them all in **Comment Manage**). The `review` element adds ratings with approval to any page. See [Concepts → History & Comments](/concepts).
"}},{"node":"website-forms","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Forms","key":"website-forms","id":"website-forms","name":"website-forms","value":"## Forms

Three ways to collect data from visitors, from zero setup to full control:

| Approach | Stores in | Use it for |
|----------|-----------|------------|
| **`form` element** dropped on a page, with fields inside | **Form Submission** (payload as JSON, form label, source page, status, spam score) | Quick forms: newsletter, quote request, RSVP |
| **Contact Form Builder** + `contact_form` element | An entity of its own, with **real columns** | Forms you'll filter, report on or process (leads, applications) |
| **Form Builder** + a controller | Whatever your code does | Custom flows |

All public submissions go through the same protection: honeypot field, fill-time check, per-IP rate limit, language-agnostic spam scoring and an optional captcha (ALTCHA proof-of-work by default, Cloudflare Turnstile optional). Suspicious submissions are kept as **Spam** silently; obvious ones are rejected. See [Security](/security).

### Contact Form Builder

1. **Contact Form Builder** → New: name, module, optional **naming series**, and the form structure (fields).
2. Saving creates a table with a column per field. The records inherit the whole submission pipeline — no controller to write.
3. Place a `contact_form` element on a page and pick the entity. Set the success message and button texts.

Each record is linked to the website it came from, and the admin is notified by email with *Reply-To* set to the submitter's email field. Review submissions in the entity's list like any other data — add a [workflow](/workflows) to triage them on a Kanban board.
"}},{"node":"website-kiosk","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Kiosk","key":"website-kiosk","id":"website-kiosk","name":"website-kiosk","value":"## Kiosk Pages

Any page of the website can also open in **kiosk** mode: `/kiosk/<link>` renders it with the app's logo and nothing else — no navigation, no footer, no way to wander off. It is meant for shared devices: a check-in screen, a station tablet, a time clock.

- The kiosk workspace is public; the page authenticates the **device** on its own (a station code, a PIN…), not with a user session.
- Kiosk pages are installable: phones and tablets can add them to the home screen and open them full screen, as an app named after the page.
"}}]}]
